cells.tense: The feeling is here, settled, and you are sitting in it without needing to move yet.
cells.ask: Take ten minutes tonight and write one thing your gut is sure of about what you want, then decide nothing after it.
cells.core:
You're sitting with what your heart holds, and you're not rushing it into anything. There's a pull toward something you can't name yet, and you're letting it stay unnamed — which is exactly what this moment asks. The feeling is stable enough to rest in, and you rest in it. That's rarer than it sounds.

Rest here isn't passive. You're not avoiding the direction; you're giving it room to make itself known, which is what it needs before it can be trusted. When you do move, it will be from something solid, not from a push. You can keep feeding this with time that isn't spent proving, planning, or solving. Nothing has to be decided for the pull to stay alive.

cells.tense: You are trying to feel the ending before it's here, and the feeling of it hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing end this week without analyzing it, announcing it, or pulling a lesson out of it — just let it end.
cells.core:
You're pushing to feel something before it's ready to be felt. The connection you're reaching toward hasn't happened yet, or the feeling hasn't settled, and you're ahead of it — testing it, checking it, trying to get the emotional result now. That pulling is making the very thing harder to feel. What's ahead can't be braced for.

What you're reaching for needs time to arrive on its own. It comes after the ending is honored, not before. The work is to stop chasing the feeling and let it show up at its own pace. One place to start: stop trying to get a resolution out of something you're still in. Letting it end on its own terms gives the change somewhere to land.

cells.tense: You have not been sitting with what the heart knows, because sitting there stopped working for you.
cells.ask: Put one feeling into plain words for yourself before you do anything with it — the first words that come, not the right ones.
cells.core:
You stopped sitting with what your heart knows, and the pull toward something better went quiet with it. There's a lot going on inside, but no way to gather it, so the direction you're steering by gets harder to see. It's not that the feeling is gone. It's that the felt sense of it lost its shape, and nothing has replaced it yet.

Forcing a feeling would only deepen the distance. What helps is gathering what's already scattered: a few honest words, a thought made whole. Small, doable, today. When your own thinking has somewhere to land, the pull can show up again. Not because you manufactured it, but because you gave it room to be recognized.

cells.tense: You are steering by a light you haven't admitted to, and the direction is doing its work right now.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're drawn toward and haven't said out loud, to someone safe, once — no explaining after.
cells.core:
You're oriented toward something — a pull, a direction, a sense of what's genuinely wanted — and you haven't named it as yours yet. It's showing up in your choices, your time, what you lean toward and what you drift from. That steering is happening right now. The saying-so isn't.

There's a simpler version of this underneath, and it's easier than it looks. You don't need to know why it matters or where it goes. You just need to put one word on the thing that's already steady in you. Saying it out loud doesn't make it more real — it makes it yours. That's the only move left here, and it's smaller than it sounds: one sentence. The direction you lean was yours to hold.
cells.sheetLine: The light's already moving you. Say where it points.

attempts.check: The record does not say this person actually sits with feeling before acting; it says the capacity is present and operating. Reverie in the Spirit house could be read as emotion misplacing itself — softness where drive belongs. The asks are still useful if the read is wrong, because each one is a small, finished act the person can do regardless of whether the diagnosis lands. The sentence that serves me more than them would be anything claiming the card means their heart is settled or that they already know the answer — that would be me interpreting the card, not describing the function.
